The buggy method is:

`org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot.initialise(java.awt.Graphics2D, java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D, org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot, java.lang.Integer, org.jfree.chart.plot.PlotRenderingInfo)`

Diagnosis:
- `PiePlot3D.draw(...)` is supposed to support a `null` dataset; it even has an explicit null/empty check later:
  - it gets the dataset,
  - checks whether it is null/empty,
  - and should draw the “no data” message and return.
- But before that null check, `PiePlot3D.draw(...)` calls `initialise(...)`.
- In `PiePlot.initialise(...)`, the code does:

```java
state.setTotal(DatasetUtilities.calculatePieDatasetTotal(plot.getDataset()));
```

- When the chart is created with a `null` dataset, `plot.getDataset()` is null here.
- So the failure happens too early, before `PiePlot3D.draw(...)` reaches its safe null-dataset handling branch.

Why this is the root cause:
- `PiePlot.getLegendItems()` already guards against `null` dataset and returns safely.
- `PiePlot3D.draw(...)` also intends to guard against `null` dataset, but the call to `initialise(...)` occurs first.
- Therefore the null handling is defeated by `PiePlot.initialise(...)`.

So the bug is essentially:
- `PiePlot.initialise(...)` assumes the dataset is non-null,
- but callers like `PiePlot3D.draw(...)` legitimately invoke it even when the dataset is null.

Best fix location:
org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot.initialise(java.awt.Graphics2D, java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D, org.jfree.chart.plot.PiePlot, java.lang.Integer, org.jfree.chart.plot.PlotRenderingInfo)
